notes: The Home Assistant Companion app for Android, on Google Play as io.homeassistant.companion.android and one of the largest actively-maintained open-source Compose codebases: :app alone declares 99 @Preview functions across settings, onboarding, Matter commissioning and the Wear-companion surfaces, with a house theme rather than stock Material. Ordinary Android Compose, single Gradle build at the repository root. One thing a reviewer should know about the build: the root build.gradle.kts calls dependencyLocking { lockAllConfigurations() } and the repository ships gradle.lockfile, so injecting the preview plugin adds modules the lock state does not describe. That is what COMPOSE_PREVIEW_WRITE_LOCKS / --write-locks in the reusable pipeline exists for; nothing is edited in the upstream checkout beyond Gradle regenerating its own lock state for the throwaway build. Licence: Apache-2.0. The build cannot configure without a google-services.json it does not commit: AndroidApplicationConventionPlugin applies the Google Services plugin to every application module, and :app died on processMinimalDebugGoogleServices before a preview was discovered. The pipeline writes a placeholder for the applicationIds named above — both flavours' debug ids are listed, so the stub survives the change of rendered variant described below. They are exact ids because the plugin does no prefix fallback, and they come from the upstream convention plugins (base io.homeassistant.companion.android, flavour suffix .minimal, build-type suffix .debug), not from guesswork. variant is fullDebug rather than the plugin's default debug. :app has minimal and full flavors, so there is no plain debug variant, and app/src/screenshotTest/ — which the preview plugin compiles, because it renders @Preview functions declared there — references SettingsWearOnboardingViewContent, a symbol that exists only in app/src/full/. minimalDebug therefore fails to compile those sources before a preview is rendered; fullDebug builds. stubGoogleServices already names the fullDebug applicationId alongside the minimal one, so the stub needs no change. Run 76 established two things. variant=fullDebug is correct: the render configured, compiled and got as far as drawing previews on the Robolectric lane, which is further than any earlier attempt. It then died two ways at once. First, :app:composePreviewRender was still making progress when the 600s default budget cancelled the build ('Build timed out after 600s, cancelling. If the build was still making progress, rerun with a longer budget'), so renderTimeout is raised to 1800 — :app here is a whole shipping application, not a design-system module. Second, one preview never reaches idle: FrontendScreen's 'Content with HTTP auth dialog' wrote the run's only .error.json, an AppNotIdleException — 'Compose did not get idle after 95819 attempts in 60 SECONDS' — which is an endlessly recomposing frame (the frontend screen hosts a WebView-backed surface), not a slow one, so no budget rescues it and it burns a minute of the budget on its own. It is excluded by a trailing wildcard rather than an exact id because the cancellation means we saw only the foldable fan-out arm; the hang is in composition and so device-independent, and an exclusion that matches nothing fails safe by rendering more. The spec names no component from this screen, so the completeness gate is unaffected.
